## 更新内容

- test(launch): remove terminal-state timing race (`075dd314`)
- fix(window): finish circular shell transitions (`eca7c58e`)
- fix(capabilities): preserve scoped analysis truth (`b29b4b47`)
- fix(settings): honest loader semantics and a user-facing platform page (`4786e847`)
  
  Follow-ups from the second device pass:
  
  - LOADER_INCOMPATIBLE fired on healthy installs: a resolved version
    chain is complete BY CONSTRUCTION (the reader throws on a missing
    parent) and self-contained loader jsons legitimately carry no
    inheritsFrom. chainComplete is no longer inferred from the parent
    count, and loader.minecraft.compatible only reports false from an
    explicit range check (future slice) — never silently.
  - Internal names are gone from the page: the evidence line shows the
    data source or the reason, never capability ids or provider ids, and
    every issue code the engine emits has a Chinese label with a generic
    fallback instead of the raw MEM_/GAME_ string.
  - The 修复板块 no longer lists registry placeholders: definitions with
    no wired provider (尚未接入检测提供方) and Action/Policy-kind
    definitions are filtered out, and rows are deduped by id defensively.
  - preflight.* / remediation.* / policy.* namespaces stay in the frozen
    registry (their providers exist) but stop flooding the page.
- fix(settings,capabilities): repair the platform page and its probe feeds (`e4978d19`)
  
  All eight real-device reports on the 平台功能 board:
  
  - Java 超时: each runtime cost one java -version process; the broker's
    3s window timed the whole java namespace out. The locator now caches
    its scan process-wide (10 min) and the broker window widens to 45s
    for first refresh — the probe round-trip drops from timeout to 1.2s.
  - 加载器版本 unknown: manifests often omit it; the version now falls
    back to the loader jar in mods/ (the same source the edit page reads).
  - 资源包 raw brackets: options.txt resourcePacks renders as a friendly
    count+names, and the settings row grows one child line per pack
    instead of bracketed JSON.
  - 陀螺仪/振动 rows list the connected controllers by name with an
    explicit per-device-channel-not-wired status instead of a bare 未知.
  - The value badge is now a gray pill, right-aligned, text centered, for
    values and unavailability alike; long reasons keep only their leading
    clause in the badge with the full text on the evidence line; enum-ish
    English values localize to Chinese.
  - Section order is a complete table (20 groups) with unknown groups
    appended instead of piling at position -1.
  - 修复板块: the preflight card renders the live report (severity,
    issue rows with Chinese labels) and its bound remediation action per
    issue, dispatching the typed remediation route.
  - mod.count finally has a producer: the mods-directory scan feeds the
    estimator's mod input (it previously read a fact nobody emitted,
    pinning every estimate at Low confidence).
  
  The parallel session's in-flight SettingsRow padding work stays out of
  this commit (saved to a WIP patch); the desktop suite runs the
  committed test set at 80 green.
- feat(jvmhost): complete observation contract (`645147a6`)
- feat(capabilities): complete planning pipeline (`3690e19f`)
- fix(architecture): register capability probe executable (`a34652f7`)
- feat(input): project recent device usage (`c2f99464`)
- feat(jvmhost): formalize launch observations (`3cc8808d`)
- feat(capabilities): add scoped planning pipeline (`866d187b`)
- feat(capabilities): environment projections and the broker derivation pass (`ad54d623`)
  
  C1+C2 of the registry gap matrix:
  
  - loader.* / account.* / java.requirement+compatibility / minecraft.settings.*
    answer from the real services: the loader from the manifest chain via
    MinecraftModLoaderDetector, accounts from the roster (offline sessions
    verified by definition, online validation honestly deferred to launch),
    java requirements from the XSR-608 resolver walking to the base
    manifest's javaVersion, settings from a new options.txt reader scoped
    to the primary instance's isolated game directory.
  - One shared primary-instance scope picks the newest instance under the
    root (10s cache) so every projection answers for the instance the user
    is about to launch.
  - The broker gains a derivation pass: cross-provider Derived capabilities
    compute after collection in registry dependency order — the sanctioned
    way to combine facts across provider ownership. Default rules cover
    platform.compatibility (native/emulated execution), memory.derived
    pressure thresholds, machine.memory classes, and java.derived.missing/
    hard_incompatible, all degrading to DependencyMissing when inputs drop.
  
  Live probe: 76 facts (was 41), all three suites green.
- fix(window): align corner and reveal masks with the rendered client area (`67c40692`)
- docs(xsr): index the capability gap matrix in the README (`21348526`)
- docs(capabilities): gap matrix of Registry 1.1 against the live implementation (`c6b54ae5`)
  
  Reads the source registry back against the 41 live facts: per-namespace
  probe gaps (jvmhost/process/formfactor/input/network/security/mod/
  resource/world/hook entirely unwired; cpu/memory/gpu/storage/filesystem/
  display/thermal/java/minecraft partial), the six-layer architecture gaps
  (no Estimator, no Policy engine, no preflight rules/aggregator/causal
  graph, no Remediation — only the Blocked⇒Verified invariant and the
  frozen namespace allowlist exist), and a dependency-driven slice order
  (C1 environment projections off existing services first, Estimator and
  Preflight engine mid, jvmhost/observation gated on the Jvm.Host
  migration).
- fix(capabilities): cross-platform audit — real probes where they exist, platform-unsupported only where none do (`b401be25`)
  
  Every provider branch now answers one of three ways per platform: a
  real probe, an honest not-yet (with the missing channel named), or
  platform-unsupported (the concept does not exist there):
  
  - macOS memory: sysctl hw.memsize for the total and
    host_statistics64 free+inactive for availability. The Windows
    commit budget has no macOS counterpart at all — commit.* reports
    PlatformUnsupported instead of a zero that preflight would misread.
  - macOS display: CGGetActiveDisplayList for count and
    CGDisplayIsBuiltin for the internal panel (the authoritative
    Apple-silicon answer), alongside the existing main-display facts.
  - Linux display: without a readable framebuffer (Wayland compositors,
    headless sessions) there is no portable per-display probe for a
    non-graphical process — that path now reports PlatformUnsupported
    instead of a generic not-implemented.
  - macOS thermal/power split from the Linux branches: hwmon and
    power_supply/cpufreq never applied to macOS; those platforms name
    their missing channels (AppleSMC, IOKit) rather than failing
    silently. GPU reasons name NVML/AMD sysfs and Metal.
  - Non-Windows memory fallback (unknown platforms) is PlatformUnsupported.
- fix(capabilities): probe the five reported machine-fact defects (`0c126011`)
  
  All five real-device reports traced to concrete defects, each fixed
  against the authoritative Windows SDK headers:
  
  - GPU adapters QI-failed everywhere: IID_IDXGIAdapter3 was written from
    memory as 645967A4-3E82-444F-... — the real idl value is
    645967A4-1392-4310-A798-8053CE3E93FD. QueryVideoMemoryInfo also sat
    on the wrong vtable slot (Adapter3's first two methods are the
    hardware-content-protection pair; the query is slot 14). The budget
    now reads live (14.94 GiB on the dev VM, stable across 20 rounds).
  - CPU temperature showed -273°C: CallNtPowerInformation carries no
    temperature at all, so its policy bytes were being decoded as
    kelvin. Windows has no driverless temperature channel — the fact now
    reports Unknown with that reason; Linux keeps hwmon.
  - Resolution showed a pixel count: the definition is a WxH string now.
  - Internal-panel detection: DisplayConfigGetDeviceInfo with
    outputTechnology INTERNAL is the authoritative signal, wired through
    GetDisplayConfigBufferSizes + QueryDisplayConfig.
  - Reflink answers by the instance volume's filesystem (ReFS on
    Windows, APFS on macOS, Btrfs/XFS on Linux; NTFS/ext4 honestly no).
  
  Fixing the panel path exposed a hard native crash: DISPLAYCONFIG_PATH_
  INFO is 80 bytes (sourceInfo + full PATH_TARGET_INFO + flags) — the
  flat 36-byte layout overflowed QueryDisplayConfig's array and seg-
  faulted the process nondeterministically. Structures now mirror
  wingdi.h exactly; the isolated probe (new --gpu/--java/--display/
  --parallel modes) and five consecutive full runs are crash-free.
- feat(capabilities): wire gpu, thermal, and power probes into the registry (`9939969c`)
  
  The last placeholder namespaces answer real OS probes now. The broker's
  ownership rule (a provider may only emit definitions it declares) shaped
  the split: gpu/thermal/power are separate providers even where one OS
  call could feed several, because a shared batch silently degraded every
  cross-owned fact to 'provider not wired'.

  machines whose display driver predates Adapter3 answer Unknown with the
  HRESULT — the Registry forbids substituting static marketing VRAM, and
  the probe run on the dev VM confirmed exactly that honest path.

  /sys/class/power_supply on Linux) plus the active scheme

  CallNtPowerInformation and hwmon, publishing sentinels as Unknown. The
  duplicate power provider from the environment slice is gone — its id
  collided and its facts moved into the hardware provider that owns them.

  composition violated: a provider may only emit facts it declares, so
  the multi-namespace mega-providers silently degraded every fact they

  JVM before its window appeared).

  providers; the root did not reach the ctor before, which is why the
  first probe run reported nothing for the path namespaces. The probe
  tool ships as a registered diagnostic project so ownership or plan
  regressions surface locally in one command.

  using), and Visual.RenderScalingProperty no longer exists publicly —

  so subscribing to Bounds covers the DPI-change reflow.

  per-frame Style calls in UpdateCard kept the whole tree perpetually
  dirty while the task page was staged — the window froze the moment an
  install started and the page opened. Cards now skip the restyle when
  the entry record is unchanged (null on first reconcile forces the full
  initial write), and a regression test locks the contract: with no entry
  change the staged page renders the cached scene, and a real change
  still produces a new one.
- fix(install,ui): throttle per-chunk progress floods and drop the vanilla button (`87791152`)
  
  Per-chunk download callbacks arrive at line speed: a fast link pushed a
  publish per 128 KiB chunk, and every publish schedules a full frame —
  the render thread drowned and the window stopped answering right up to
  the moment an install failed. Install and launch-completion reports now
  step by at least 0.2% of the whole job, capping publish volume at ~500
  per run regardless of link speed. A regression test locks the other
  freeze class: after a failed install the idle tree must render the
  cached scene unchanged (reference-equal), so no per-frame dirty writer
  survives the failure.
  
  The 使用原版 Minecraft button is gone — not selecting a loader already
  means vanilla. The ui.install.loader.vanilla intent stays: the catalog
  flow and its tests use it as the explicit reset-to-vanilla selection.
- fix(launch): one progress clock inside file completion (`72273d9a`)
  
  With real progress flowing from the completion stage, the coordinator's
  soft heartbeat kept racing it: the heartbeat climbs to its 65.45%
  ceiling in ~1.4s while real repair progress crawls from 34% — the card
  flickered between the two for the whole stage. Stages that publish
  their own progress now opt out of the heartbeat (complete_files does),
  and the repair reports per-byte progress with a speed line, so the bar
  moves continuously through large single files instead of stepping per
  file.
- fix(launch): report file completion progress on the 0..1 scale (`8f9c65ca`)
  
  The completion stage published raw stage weights (LoginWeight +
  CompleteFilesWeight × fraction = 15..30) where the progress contract
  expects a 0..1 fraction — everything past 0.52 clamped to 1.0, so the
  launching card flashed 100% mid-repair before the coordinator heartbeat
  (ceiling 65.45%) pulled it back. The same absolute-value mistake made
  the install card jump to 100% at the 版本信息 boundary and crash back
  near zero on the first transfer. Both now report fractions, and a
  recorder locks the band: never past the stage ceiling, never regressing.
- fix(tasks): finished entries read as fully complete; id reuse replaces the card (`9c926f8e`)
  
  Terminal states never carried Progress=1, so a finished card could read
  50% forever; completion now reads as 100% while canceled keeps the
  progress it reached. Abandoned registrations release their id — reuse
  replaces the failed card with a fresh running one under the same id,
  which the contract test now locks. Also closes the one-file lag in the
  install progress count.
  
  The local dotnet-run wrapper was swallowing suite crashes (summary line
  with zero PASS lines, exit 0); gates now run the built exe directly.
- fix(install): count every transferred file and report the closing count (`65a95fc1`)
  
  The deduplicated transfer list counts each destination once, but the
  progress callback fires mid-download, so the card froze one file short
  (3/4 at completion) — the flake CI caught. A final report closes the
  file count before the task completes.
- fix(launch,install): repair missing files before the JVM starts and stop the UI render spin (`59c8eafb`)
  
  Three real-device failures traced to one root: the legacy 补全文件 step was
  never migrated, and half-installed instances were discoverable.
  
  - complete_files now verifies every referenced file on disk and repairs
    the missing ones through the shared download engine (client jar, asset
    index, asset objects, the whole inheritance chain's libraries). A
    missing library used to kill the JVM before its window appeared — the
    opaque 'JVM 在窗口出现前意外退出'.
  - Installs commit their version documents LAST: discovery lists
    instances by the version json, so a run that dies mid-transfer leaves
    an invisible, resumable directory instead of a launchable half-install.
    A single 403 (bmclapi rate limit, real-network verified at 99%) now
    gets one delayed retry, and third-party library lists keep the
    canonical URL as a last-resort source.
  - Success closes the launching page immediately — the user returns to
    the library while the game warms up instead of parking on a
    游戏已启动 card until the session ends.
  - The task bubble and cards no longer MarkDirty unconditionally at
    FramePreparing: the perpetual dirty flag kept every scene commit
    changing, spinning the render loop — startup froze with no frame
    painted, and backing out during an install froze the same way. All
    per-frame work is now change-guarded.
  - External cancellation of an install returns a Cancelled result
    instead of letting the raw exception escape the route.
- fix(tests): restore the install pipeline assertions mangled by a message-strip regex (`ec54592b`)
  
  The regex that dropped per-call assert messages from the new install
  tests also ate trailing path arguments out of multi-line Path.Combine
  calls, so the suite asserted directories instead of the written files
  (and an earlier stale build let that slip through locally). The paths
  are restored; each new test now passes with a fresh build.
- feat(install): run real installs through the task center (`6758e959`)

  placeholder warning. MinecraftInstallService resolves the vanilla version
  JSON from the Mojang manifest (bmclapi failover) and the Fabric-family
  loader profile, writes both version documents before any transfer so a
  partial install stays inspectable, plans every file through the shared
  planners (asset index, client jar, platform-filtered libraries, assets,
  catalog-resolved addon jars into mods/), and downloads through the shared
  DownloadService with resume and segmentation. The whole run is one
  task-center task with file-accurate progress; completion fires Installed
  and the composition root rescans the active version library.
  
  Processor-based loaders (Forge, NeoForge, …) are rejected before touching
  disk with an explicit not-yet-migrated message — processor execution
  stays deferred per XSR-604. Metadata and byte transfer are ports, so the
  pipeline is covered by in-memory fakes without network.

  (progress, speed, remaining files) with a bulk clear-finished action, the
  body presents one card per entry — state icon, stage copy, progress fill,

  The legacy extra dock's task bubble returns as a persistent shell-level
  overlay: a round button in the bottom-right dock inset whose translucent
  fill rises from the bottom edge with aggregated task progress, hidden
  while the task page owns the corner, filled at 100% once all tasks are
  done so completion is acknowledged rather than timed out. XsrUiProgress
  gains the Bottom fill anchor for the rising fill; runtime-built entities
  set presentation-only targets through the new SetTarget so the backend
  catch-up animation still applies. Reconciliation stays on the render
  thread: workers only publish the wake cell, all tree mutations happen at
  FramePreparing.
- feat(tasks): add the task center service contract (`512f0a55`)
  
  Foundation-owned background task tracking for installs and downloads,
  parity with the legacy task manager: entries stay visible until
  dismissed, stage steps never move backwards when a later phase reuses a

- fix(probe): validate the property contract; drop the self-drawn window shadow (`43354f46`)

  a malformed or hostile client can publish a format-8 property under the same
  name, and the unconditional 8-byte read was both an over-wide read and a PID
  mismatch risk. The read now demands CARDINAL/type with format 32 (host long
  on LP64), reads exactly one element via ReadIntPtr, and treats everything
  else as absent. The xvfb smoke's own XChangeProperty had the mirror-image
  bug — it wrote int[] where format 32 requires host long[] — so the test that
  proves the ABI was itself violating it.

  probe path (and its ABI) is the product's shipping target, and it was only
  ever exercised on CoreCLR.

  transparency is not guaranteed on every Windows machine; when it fails, the
  shadow paints over an opaque margin and exposes the rectangular window
  bounds. The margin stays as a transparent buffer and XSR-703 now documents
  the three size meanings (native outer, chrome surface, semantic viewport) so
  acceptance tests name the one they measure.

  takes a coherent snapshot before activation and the old mirror is

  state.

  layout, and pointer or keyboard activation emits bound commands as
  intent with renderer-produced correlation IDs. The navigator owns a
  page stack as pure tree operations, the stage draws overlays above the
  page by attach order, and every scene node carries role, label, text,
  and focus state for backend accessibility bridges.
- feat(ui-next): add deterministic layout and scene production (`662a0fa5`)
  
  Layout runs measure/arrange over dirty subtrees only, so a single leaf
  change re-aggregates just its ancestor chain and the visit count makes
  that observable. The scene is an immutable depth-first draw list with
  semantic roles and state-bound text, and a clean tree reuses the cached
  scene without advancing the version. Backends receive exactly this
  scene; they never see entities or components.
- feat(ui-next): start wave 2 with entity kernel (`34a2e287`)
  
  The renderer owns a deterministic entity-component tree: attach-order
  children, cycle-safe hierarchy edits, a closed component set, dirty
  flags that bubble subtree state precisely, and a state bridge that
  marks exactly the entities bound to a changed state entry. The narrow
  boundary is frozen on the Wave 1 kernel: UI.Next reads XsrStateStore
  and emits commands through its own intent sink, never touching
  services, runtimes, or backends.
- fix(xsr): correct derived invalidation, scheduler lifetime, add scopes (`bee1fa4d`)
  
  Derived-state invalidation compared per-entry revisions across
  dependencies, which are local counters, so a dependency with a low
  revision could change without invalidating a derived entry. Applied
  mutations now allocate a store-global change stamp and dependency
  watermarks use it; compute results commit only when no dependency
  mutation crossed the computation window, including the first
  computation, and retries stay bounded.
  
  Scheduled work now follows an explicit state machine serialized under
  the scheduler gate, and the scheduler owns every timer, so zero-due-time
  callbacks cannot leak one and disposing a work handle is safe before,
  during, or after the scheduler's own disposal. Lifecycle observers now
  run outside the transition gate.
  
  Runtime lifetime scopes arrive as their own abstraction, distinct from
  event ordering scopes: plugins, windows, and sessions own a scope whose
  single dispose releases owned resources and child scopes exactly once.

- feat(xsr): add scheduling, lifecycle, and session diagnostics (`4a9db78e`)
  
  Scheduled work is cancellable, TimeProvider-driven, and always observed,
  so detached work never produces unobserved exceptions. Lifecycle is a
  guarded forward-only state machine that rejects illegal transitions and
  serializes competing ones. A bounded session trace correlates dispatch,
  state, events, scheduling, and lifecycle observations under one session
  ID, preserving correlation IDs wherever the subsystem contract carries
  them, and services reject wrong-phase operations with the stable
  xsr.lifecycle error.
- feat(xsr): add ordered event scopes with bounded delivery (`bce2fa76`)
  
  One declared scope is one ordering domain: all events routed into it
  share a contiguous sequence and one bounded ring, so cross-event order
  is total. Delivery is a pull-based cursor that never blocks publication;
  when a live subscriber still needs the oldest retained record, a full
  scope rejects publication with the stable backpressure error instead of
  dropping events, and replay from the retained window lets consumers
  catch up.
- feat(xsr): add revisioned state with derived dependency graph (`7a680f05`)
  
  State entries declared through the sealed registry carry monotonic
  revisions and availability separate from their last value, so readers
  always see coherent applied state. Collection deltas apply only against
  a matching base revision and otherwise demand a snapshot refresh, and
  derived entries recompute only after an input revision changes. The
  deterministic sealed registry moves into the abstractions kernel so
  routing, state, events, and generated code resolve one identical
  mapping.
- feat(xsr): add command and query routing with stable errors (`840f3ad2`)
  
  Commands separate acceptance from asynchronous completion, and every
  completion is observed even when the caller detaches. Queries apply
  caller cancellation and an optional routing timeout. Runtime failures
  cross the boundary as stable XSR error codes so handler exceptions and
  CLR type names never leak into the public contract.
